production.note: US model years 2022 and 2023: Cars.com lists Kona N model years '2023' and '2022' only. KBB's first-look article covers the '2022 Hyundai Kona N' (kbb-kona-n-debut-2021). The next-generation Kona launched for 2024 without an N version. End year rests on databases (see provisionalNote).

displacementL.note: '2.0-liter'. No opened page prints the cc figure; Cars.com lists '2.0 L/122' (cars-com-2022-kona-n).

fuel.note: Inferred: gasoline turbocharged engine with no hybrid system.

drivetrain.note: '8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission sends power to the front wheels'; Cars.com: 'Front Wheel Drive'.

transmission.note: '8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission'; Autoblog: 'Hyundai's familiar eight-speed dual-clutch automated manual' (autoblog-kona-n-first-drive). No manual in the US.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Its 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four pumps out 276 horsepower and 289 pound-feet of torque" (James Riswick). KBB (Sean Tucker): "turbocharged, 2.0-liter 4-cylinder engine making 276 horsepower" (kbb-kona-n-debut-2021). Cars.com: "SAE Net Horsepower @ RPM 276 @ 6000". N Grin Shift gives a 20-second boost: "Output is cranked up to 286 hp" (Autoblog). No Hyundai page advertising the 286 hp figure was opened, so the record uses 276 hp, as the Elantra N record does for the same engine and feature.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL. 2022 Kona N, 8-speed DCT (the only configuration). Autoblog (James Riswick): "Putting that much power in such a small car (3,340 pounds) is as uproariously fun as you'd hope". Cars.com gives the same: "Base Curb Weight 3,340 lbs" (cars-com-2022-kona-n). One article and one database.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 3,340 lb rests on one article (Autoblog) and one database (Cars.com). The end year (2023) rests on Cars.com's model-year list. A Hyundai Motor America specification sheet or brochure with a curb weight (the 2023 US Kona brochure could not be opened: rate-limited) would replace them; it would also settle whether Hyundai advertises the 286 hp N Grin Shift figure.
